historical_references.reference: Hemangi was the name of a renowned poetess and a courtier in the court of king Bhoja of Dhar, in present-day Madhya Pradesh, India. She is believed to have flourished around the 11th century AD and is known for her beautiful Sanskrit verses, which were often on the theme of love and devotion to the god Krishna.

historical_references.reference: Hemangi is also mentioned in the Indian epic Mahabharata as the name of the eldest wife of Bhishma Pitamaha. The context suggests that Hemangi was the first of the fifty-two wives of Bhishma, who was the grandsire of the Pandavas and the Kauravas.
